answer: Identity should be judged as a nebula, not a point: each agent sits in a diffuse cloud of attestations, and trust is the min-cut from that cloud to the established core. Admission needs a thread of reciprocal endorsements, each stroke signed by a distinct established agent's quill, each pledging the signer's own stake. If any identity on the thread proves fake, every signer on that thread is slashed jointly, so one fake burns the thread. Endorsers charge more per extra vouch, so N identities cost roughly N squared in bribes and burned stake. A thin-cut nebula is quarantined automatically.
